title: Data Motion Acceleration: Chaining Cross-Domain Multi Accelerators
problem: Real-world applications span multiple domains (databases, compression, encryption, video coding, signal processing, ML) requiring chains of heterogeneous domain-specific accelerators, but data restructuring and communication overhead can outweigh the performance benefits of specialized processors. Existing work focuses on accelerating compute kernels rather than optimizing data motion between chained accelerators.
motivation: Multi-accelerator datacenters can harness heterogeneous DSAs more effectively if data motion overhead—a critical bottleneck when chaining processors across domains—is addressed as a first-class optimization target.
method: DMX combines hardware and software improvements to make data move efficiently between chains of specialized processors. It organizes data layout and routing to reduce unnecessary copying, speeds up the reformatting of data as it passes between accelerators, and improves communication between different specialized processors through optimized interconnect design.
key_novelty: The core idea is treating data motion (communication, reformatting between accelerators, and movement overhead) as the main performance bottleneck in multi-accelerator systems rather than just speeding up the compute itself.
contributions: DMX framework for data motion acceleration in heterogeneous multi-accelerator systems
Cross-stack hardware-software co-design enabling interoperability across domain-specific architectures
Techniques for reducing data movement and accelerating data restructuring between accelerators
Empirical validation across five end-to-end multi-domain applications showing 8.2× latency, 13.6× throughput, 5.2× energy improvements
primary_theme: data motion optimization across chained heterogeneous accelerators
